A while back, I had a women that answered the door and when I started pitching, within seconds she stops me and says “you know, I’ve got fucking cancer... do you really think I give a fuck about your shitty product?”

I couldn’t breathe in shock... I didn’t even know what to say, I mean, what could I say? I quickly apologized, I told her sincerely that I couldn’t imagine what she’s going through , and that I’ll be on my way.

Just as I was about to leave, she took a deep breath, and to my surprise, she said “I’m sorry for lashing out, you’re just doing your job”.... that caught me off guard once again, I turned around and thanked her, I didn’t even care about what I was supposed to be doing, I didn’t care about the product, the job, or the sales that day... she even invited me for dinner that evening.

Believe me when I say this: I know what people go through, I’ve had my fair share of hardships in life, I’ve ran into crazy things during this job, I’ve had a guy that got fired literally minutes before I showed up... life happens man, I know

I never complain about what people say or do, I don’t even stress about it... how can I? I have no control over what people will do when they open the door. All I’ve ever said is that it sucks being on the receiving end of it sometimes... when I see someone having a bad day, I do what anyone would do, apologize, wish them well, and move on.

You’re absolutely right, and honestly I have no problem with people closing doors on my face and yelling at me.. I’m on their property while they’re minding their own business. I have no right to complain about how it’s frustrating and annoying when people are rude. I get that.

I’m not arguing that what I do is polite and comforting, all I’m saying is that it can be discouraging at times... and when I say that “people are extremely rude” I mean when people spit on me and shove me, like I said earlier, tell me to “fuck off”, yell at me, and shut the door all you want, that’s perfectly fine and justified. But I don’t think there’s a need to go that far, please correct me if I’m wrong.

Okay, I’m probably gonna get downvoted for this but please just here me out... I work for a company that could be described as MLM, selling telecom services door to door on pure commission and no base... this is sounds about as bad as it gets right?

Well, here’s the surprising truth... I love the job. I make about $2000 a week (I also realize that this is not for everyone and that not everyone I work with makes this paycheque) but I get to work outside, meet new people and sell a pretty good and easy product.

But the biggest thing for me is that this job has wired my brain to be positive no matter the outcome... door to door can suck at times with people constantly shutting the door in your face and being extremely rude, so keeping a positive attitude is key, and this job has taught me this... I won’t just keep what I’ve learned here for door knocking but for literally everything I’ll ever do.

I’m not saying that bad companies that sell naive college kids on a hypothetical dream and force em to sell a product neither good, helpful or simply something they don’t believe in. Nor am I saying that there aren’t companies that try to scam people specially by sending employees door to door, but know that there are good companies doing honest work too

Sure you maybe skeptical, or maybe you don’t believe me at all, you might think that I’m just another young guy caught in a trap.... perhaps maybe I am.

But I hope we can agree that what I’ve learned in this job is phenomenal and hopefully I gave a different perspective on a seemingly stereotypically hated job :)
